Fixed. Committed as 3c302be on fix/cluster2-mission-layers (not pushed — you push per your instructions).

**Fix**: `Store.conflictScanIDs` (internal/mission/store.go:1901) now collects the audit-owned tail into a local `[]string`, sorts it with `sort.Strings`, then appends to `ids`. Kept your recommended approach — sort only the tail, preserving "repo tree first, then audit-owned" grouping — rather than sorting the whole result; the repo-tree half is already deterministic via `os.ReadDir`, so sorting it too would be a no-op that just obscures which half changed.

**Regression test**: `TestStore_ConflictScanIDsAuditOwnedTailIsSorted` (store_test.go). Used the "call repeatedly, assert identical to first" form you specified — 5 audit-owned IDs (5! = 120 orderings, not the minimal 2) via 50 iterations of `conflictScanIDs()`, asserting `assert.Equal(t, first, got)` each time.

Verified both directions manually before committing:
- Pre-fix (reverted the sort to the bare `for id := range owned { ids = append(...) }` form): failed on iteration 1 — actual diff showed `[943 944 940 941 942]` vs expected `[940 941 942 943 944]`. Reliably red, not flaky-red.
- Post-fix: 50/50 iterations identical, PASS.

**Pattern audit**: checked every `for x := range someMap { ... append(...) }` in internal/mission. Found only this one instance. Everything else that ranges into a slice ranges over a slice already (contracts, entries, events, roles from `ListRoles`) — one of those (store.go ~2691, worker/evaluator role-overlap detection) even has a precedent comment: "Sort by name so map-iteration order in the lister cannot leak into the output" (hash.go), confirming this exact defect class was caught and fixed there before. Nothing else needs a fix — "nothing else" is the answer.

**Gates**:
- `make check`: green (vet, staticcheck, shellcheck, markdownlint, validate-content, `go test -race ./...` all pass).
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`: exit 0.
- Detached gate (`git archive HEAD` into `.tmp/hc`, `setsid env -u CLAUDE_PID ... go test ./... -count=1` piped through `tee`): 27 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 no-test-files (`internal/repomiss`) — matches your expected count exactly.

No CHANGELOG entry — this is an internal ordering fix with no user-visible behavior change (the conflict *set* was always correct; only display order of an already-nondeterministic internal list is now stable). Say if you want one anyway for audit-trail purposes.

Files: `<repo>/internal/mission/store.go`, `<repo>/internal/mission/store_test.go`

tool_input.body:
Fixed in `3c302be`. Confirmed the whole path before fixing rather than taking the report at face value: the randomized slice reaches `checkWriteSetConflicts`, whose `[]Conflict` goes to `formatConflictError` (`conflict.go:539`), which joins one line per conflict in slice order. So an operator hitting two or more audit-owned conflicts sees the same conflicts reordered run to run. The conflict *set* is unaffected — this is a legibility defect, not a correctness one.

Sorted the tail only, not the whole result. The repo-tree half is already deterministic via `os.ReadDir`, and keeping "repo tree first, then audit-owned" preserves the grouping the function intends while confining the diff to the actual defect.

Two things beyond the one-line fix:

**The regression test is built to be reliably red, not flaky-red.** The theoretical minimum to expose this is two IDs, but at two IDs a pre-fix run passes half the time. The test uses five (120 orderings) and compares 51 calls against the first, so a false pass needs randomization to pick the same order 51 times running. A test that only *sometimes* catches the bug it was written for is not a gate.

**Audited the class, not the instance.** Swept `internal/mission` for the same map-range-into-slice shape reaching operator output or a test assertion — no other instance. Worth stating explicitly, since "no other occurrences" is a finding and not an absence of one.

This one is a good catch precisely because it is invisible locally: map randomization means it can pass every run on one machine and reorder on another, which is the same shape as the environment-dependent failure that made this branch's earlier rounds necessary.

tool_input.message:
Round 6 on PR #508 — two stale-comment findings from Copilot, both verified real by me before sending. Same worktree and branch; `3c302be` is pushed and green.

**I1 — `conflictScanIDs` doc comment, `internal/mission/store.go` ~1853 and ~1873.** Two stale claims, both about `repoMissionIDs`:

- ~1853: "it scans `<repoRoot>/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/*/audit.jsonl` for contract_id references". Round 3 added sealed-chunk scanning (`audit-<first>-<last>.jsonl`) and round 4 added the live tail under `checkoutRoot`. The comment describes the round-1 behavior.
- ~1873: "Cost: repoMissionIDs reads every audit.jsonl line under every session this repo has ever recorded." Same staleness, and it now also understates the cost — the scan covers sealed chunks and two roots. Fix the cost paragraph to match what the code actually reads, don't just swap the filename.

**I2 — `internal/mission/syncdir_unix.go:14`.** The comment names `TestWriteContractFile_SyncDirFailurePropagates`; the test is `TestWriteContractFile_SyncDirFailureIsWarnedNotErrored`. This is worse than a dangling name: "Propagates" asserts the opposite of the current contract, which round 3 changed to warn-and-return-nil because the rename is the commit point. A reader trusting the comment learns the wrong durability contract. Fix the name and make sure the surrounding prose states the actual contract.

Both are comment-only — no behavior change, so no new tests. But before you commit, sweep the rest of the round-2/3/4 diff for the same class: any comment or doc line still describing pre-round behavior of `repoMissionIDs`, `syncDir`, `writeContract`, or the lock unification, and any reference to a renamed or deleted test. Copilot found two; I want to know whether there are more rather than absorbing another round. Report what you found, including "nothing else" if that's the answer. Check DES-075's amendments too — if the ADR prose carries the same stale description, it matters more there than in a code comment.

`make check` green, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0, and the detached gate before reporting. Commit, do not push — I push.

For context on why I'm not waving these through as cosmetic: this is the `ethos-lldo` class, the first bug in the whole triage — a comment describing a code path the code no longer takes, steering the reader away from where the real behavior lives. I cited that class in a review reply one thread earlier and then failed to catch these two in my own review of rounds 3 and 4. The class is worth a sweep.
